around.headline: Kingpin of Bengaluru's spurious/fake medicine racket arrested at airport after fleeing to Sharjah
around.summary: The absconding kingpin of a fake/spurious drug racket was arrested at Bengaluru airport after landing from Sharjah, having evaded police for over a month, per The Hindu and Deccan Herald. Buy medicines only from licensed pharmacies and check the strip's manufacturer and batch details, especially for chronic-illness or high-value drugs.

around.headline: Elderly man killed by wild elephant near BM Kaval forest on Mysuru Road
around.summary: An elderly man was trampled to death by a wild elephant during his morning walk near BM Kaval forest on Mysuru Road, in Bengaluru South, per Deccan Herald and The Hindu. Avoid walking alone near forest-fringe stretches on the city's outskirts early morning or at dusk, when elephant movement is more likely.

around.headline: BMTC launches 'Namma BMTC App 2.0' with integrated bus and metro ticketing
around.summary: BMTC has rolled out an upgraded app that combines bus and metro ticketing in one place, per This Week India. Commuters juggling both networks can now buy a single pass instead of separate bus and metro tickets.

around.headline: AI traffic camera mistakes guitar case for helmetless pillion rider, fines Bengaluru man
around.summary: A Bengaluru man riding solo with a guitar case strapped behind him was fined Rs 500 after an AI traffic camera misread the case as an unhelmeted passenger, per Deccan Chronicle and Hindustan Times. Wrongly issued e-challans like this can be disputed online with photo evidence, so don't just pay without checking the violation photo first.

around.headline: Karnataka minister rules out load-shedding despite drought-driven power shortage
around.summary: Even as a weak monsoon pushes up power demand and the state secures 85 lakh tonnes of extra coal, the energy minister has ruled out scheduled load-shedding, per TOI Bengaluru. Residents can expect regular supply for now, though it's still sensible to avoid running heavy appliances during evening peak hours.

around.headline: Sensex and Nifty plunge, Nifty Bank sheds over 1,000 points in Monday's market crash
around.summary: Indian equity benchmarks fell sharply on Monday, with the Nifty Bank index dropping more than 1,000 points, per Upstox. If you hold mutual funds, SIPs or direct equity, avoid panic-selling on a single bad session — check the specific factors behind the fall before reacting.

street_smart.title: It's late and you need cash. The only ATM around is a standalone, unguarded kiosk on a quiet stretch — no bank branch, no security guard, no one else in line. As you walk up, you notice the card-slot edge looks slightly loose and there's a thin, faintly discoloured film stuck over part of the keypad. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Evergreen rotation (credit/debit card skimming) — no single incident in today's feeds gave a personal, choice-based trap (today's real Bengaluru stories — a fake-medicine-racket arrest, a fatal elephant attack, an AI camera misfiring a challan, and a market crash — are either law-enforcement wins, tragedies, or not personal decision points). This mechanism hasn't appeared as a Daily Pulse street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: Skimmers are thin plastic or metal overlays fitted over a genuine card slot to copy your card's magnetic-stripe data, often paired with a hidden pinhole camera or a fake keypad overlay to capture your PIN. A rigged machine can look almost identical to a normal one, and it still dispenses cash normally, so most victims don't notice anything wrong until unauthorised transactions show up later.

choices.text: It's a real bank-branded ATM in a public spot — use it as usual, since tampering this obvious would surely have been reported and removed by now.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Skimmers are deliberately built to look unremarkable and are often installed and removed within hours, long before anyone reports them. A visibly loose slot or an odd film over the keypad is exactly the kind of tampering skimmers require — 'it looks mostly normal' is not a safety check.

choices.text: Wiggle the card slot and keypad panel to see if they're loose, then just shield your hand while entering the PIN and go ahead.
choices.feedback: Risky. A wiggle test can catch a crude, poorly fitted skimmer, but well-made ones are glued or clipped on tightly enough to pass this check, and a hidden pinhole camera above the keypad can still capture your PIN even with your hand shielding the keys from the side. A physical check is a good habit, but it isn't reliable enough on its own once you've already spotted a specific red flag.

choices.text: Walk away and use a different ATM instead — ideally one inside a bank branch, a guarded kiosk, or a well-lit, busy location.
choices.feedback: Correct. Once a machine shows any sign of tampering, the safest move is to simply not use it — no physical check can fully rule out a well-hidden skimmer or camera. Bank-branch and guarded ATMs are checked and monitored far more often, which is why they're the safer default, especially at night.

choices.text: Use the ATM, but immediately check your bank statement over the next few days for any unfamiliar transactions.
choices.feedback: Risky. Checking your statement afterwards only helps you catch fraud after your card details are already stolen — by then the skimmed data may have been cloned and used, and disputing the charges takes time and effort. Prevention (avoiding a tampered machine) is far better than after-the-fact detection.

takeaways: A loose card slot, an odd film or overlay on the keypad, or a wobbly panel near the screen are all signs of possible tampering — treat any one of them as reason enough to walk away, not just to be extra careful.
Prefer ATMs inside bank branches, malls or guarded/well-lit locations, especially at night — they're checked and monitored far more often than standalone kiosks.

Enable SMS/app alerts for every card transaction so you're notified within seconds of any unauthorised use, and report a suspected skimming or fraud immediately via your bank's app, its 24x7 helpline, or the national cyber-crime helpline 1930.

quiz.question: The kingpin of a Bengaluru fake/spurious medicine racket was arrested at the airport today after landing from where?
quiz.why: He had been absconding for over a month before being caught on arrival, per Deccan Herald — a reminder to always buy medicines from licensed pharmacies and check batch and manufacturer details.

quiz.question: Where in Bengaluru was an elderly man killed by a wild elephant during his morning walk today?
options: Near BM Kaval forest on Mysuru Road
quiz.why: Human-elephant conflict incidents cluster around forest-fringe stretches on the city's outskirts, which is why walking alone near these areas at dawn or dusk carries real risk.

quiz.question: By how much did the Nifty Bank index drop in Monday's market plunge, per today's report?
quiz.why: Sharp single-day falls like this are a reason to avoid panic-selling SIPs or mutual fund holdings — it's worth understanding the specific trigger before reacting to one bad session.

quiz.question: Which constitutional body is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India, including resolving disputes like party symbol allotment?
quiz.why: The Election Commission is an independent constitutional authority under Article 324, separate from the judiciary and the executive, precisely so elections stay insulated from the ruling party of the day.

quiz.question: In India, GST (Goods and Services Tax) is best described as what kind of tax?
options: An indirect tax collected on the sale of goods and services
A direct tax on personal income
A one-time wealth tax on assets
A tax levied only on imports
quiz.why: Because GST is built into the price of what you buy and collected by the seller on the government's behalf, its burden ultimately falls on the end consumer, unlike income tax, which is paid directly by the earner.
